pairs.registryProposal: tool-identity-vs-tool-name is written from the publisher's side. Here the consumer persists usage for tools from third-party MCP servers that publish no identifier at all (src-tauri/src/engine/mcp_tools.rs:941 records the bare wire name). The technique should say what a consumer stores when the wire carries no identifier: mint a local identity at first sight, keyed on the registration plus the name, and record renames as events. The repo's own attempt at this, mcp:{credential_id}:{tool_name}, is still a name.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/db/src/repos/resources/mcp_gateways.rs:48 add_member accepts a duplicate display_name in the same gateway; collision management is a convention in a doc comment (src/api/credentials/mcpGateways.ts:44 'Keep short and unique') rather than a constraint, and the shadowed member's tools become unreachable or misrouted
